decisions.reason: The accelerator program is the furthest from the firm's core machinery-and-plant business, so in a growing but hardware-focused company its resources would likely be redirected to scalable recycling technologies and R&D projects.

Despite being less directly aligned with the firm's equipment base, the CO2-negative binder has been framed as a strategic flagship and fits an R&D-intensive growth path, so management would likely continue supporting it.
The infectious waste decontamination plant is close to the established offer, prominently positioned, and well suited to the firm's modular treatment model, making withdrawal unlikely.

The mobile mechanical recycling plant is highly consistent with the firm's decentralized recycling strategy, manufacturing capabilities, and target customers, so it is very likely to remain on the market.
